text: Twenty-point-nine million barrels a day through one strait — a fifth of everything the world burns. On Friday it all looks boring — Brent settles at seventy-two.
Then it happens — on a Saturday, markets closed. So Monday opens four fifty-two higher, six-point-two percent.
It spikes to eighty-two… then closes four under — whoever chased it bought the top.
So here's the whole method: don't chase, don't predict — the crisis already picked the direction. The pattern just picks your moment — and the price where you're wrong.
Then it coils — one day entirely inside the last. A close above the range triggers it — stop below.
And it hits — two sessions later. Then the war premium bleeds away — seventy dollars by July.
But one winner is just a story — it fired seventeen times, and reached target four.
And here's the test: July. Another attack, another spike — same pattern, four sessions later, target again.
That's why it works mostly in a crisis — the market leans one way, and the break follows through.
